A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MoDGS. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial reformatting and added material.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction experiments, quantitative benchmark results in Tables 1–2, ablations in Table 3, and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds benchmark results, Shape-of-Motion comparisons, and several quantitative ablation and robustness studies.

M1.justification: The canonical Gaussians, invertible deformation field, 3D-aware initialization, and ordinal-loss formulation remain substantially unchanged. Section 3.2 adds SAM2 segmentation as an alternative to flow thresholding for selecting static regions during depth-scale initialization; it does not establish which experiments used this option.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates DyNeRF, Nvidia, and the self-collected MCV dataset. v2 additionally evaluates DAVIS natural videos, including animal and outdoor scenes with recovered camera poses (Appendix A.6 and Figure 11), substantially extending its benchmark coverage beyond the original datasets.

E2.justification: The principal SC-GS, Deformable-GS, HexPlane, and RoDynRF comparisons remain. v2 adds evaluated comparisons with Shape-of-Motion, prior depth-ranking losses, and depth-supervised HexPlane (Tables 3, 8, and 10), providing substantially broader controls for reconstruction quality and the proposed loss.

E3.justification: The reported initialization and joint-training budgets each fall from 30k to 20k steps. Quantitative evaluation expands from five to six DyNeRF scenes and three to eight Nvidia scenes, while new experiments introduce DAVIS pose recovery and controlled loss, noise, and initialization settings. Retained camera splits and metrics are unchanged; the budget revision alone does not establish that retained results were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendices A.7–A.13 add tests of alpha sensitivity, depth-noise robustness, ranking-loss alternatives, video-depth supervision, depth-supervised HexPlane, and zero-deformation versus Kaiming initialization. These investigate several previously untested explanations and dependencies. The earlier initialization, Pearson-loss, and depth-warping analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests. The Gaussian distribution parameters in v2 Table 5 specify injected depth noise, not uncertainty in experimental estimates.

E6.justification: All 96 overlapping per-scene metric entries and the original three-row ablation table are unchanged. v2 adds substantial results for additional scenes, comparators, and analyses. MoDGS's Nvidia average PSNR changes from 23.27 to 19.27 and DyNeRF from 22.90 to 22.64 because the evaluated scene sets expand; these are not same-setting performance declines. Reported training time and rendering speed also change under the revised training budget.

T1.justification: The ordinal indicator drops its explicit equal-depth case between v1 Equation 3 and v2 Equation 2. Appendix A.5 also adds a derivation showing that the summed squared standardized rendered depths equal the pixel count, supporting a step merely asserted in v1's Pearson-equivalence argument. No new theorem or broader theoretical framework is introduced.

C1.justification: The central claims remain novel-view synthesis from casual monocular videos through 3D-aware initialization and ordinal depth supervision, with advantages over existing DVS methods. Additional evaluations support these retained contributions without materially redefining their scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds specular-reflection failures and a current video-length limit of approximately ten seconds, with longer videos proposed as requiring greater model capacity and training. It also explains alpha sensitivity and ranking-loss behavior. Existing limitations concerning unseen regions, training cost, and dependence on depth estimates remain.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents one-in-five flow keyframes, scene and depth normalization, exclusion of depth pairs differing by at most 0.02, Gaussian-center depth rendering, and Kaiming initialization. It also supplies DAVIS preprocessing instructions and promises future code release. These additions improve documentation without establishing that every newly disclosed implementation choice changed.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion adds an ordinal-depth lineage including Zoran, Fu, Chen, and Pavlakos, and distinguishes MoDGS's dense rendered-depth supervision from earlier approaches. It also positions MoDGS against concurrent DG-Marbles, Shape-of-Motion, and MoSca, emphasizing its use of pairwise RAFT flow rather than strong long-range correspondences.

P1.justification: v2 corrects the title spelling, edits terminology and several paragraphs, renames headings, and moves implementation details into Appendix A.1. The main introduction–related work–method–experiments–conclusion narrative remains recognizable; much of the additional prose accompanies new scientific content.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout. Figure 1 is redesigned, comparison figures gain input-view columns, and the initialization figure is rearranged. Dataset summaries are consolidated into a main-text table while expanded per-scene tables move to the appendix, alongside new figures and analysis tables.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence for the central contributions through fuller benchmark coverage, Shape-of-Motion comparisons, and targeted loss, depth-supervision, robustness, and initialization controls. These address important gaps in v1's comparative evidence, supported by clearer implementation details and applicability limits. The gains outweigh localized reporting problems: the Nvidia D-GS summary disagrees with the displayed per-scene mean, and Table 9's metric improvements are less consistent than its accompanying interpretation suggests.
